newsitem.title: Russia: Yeltsin tells Kremlin team to halt "verbal duels".
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells Kremlin team to halt "verbal duels".

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday told rivals in the Kremlin and the government to stop "verbal duels" over their positions on breakaway Chechnya, press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.

He told a news conference that Yeltsin had ordered Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, security tsar Alexander Lebed and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov to reach a consensus on Chechnya before closed parliamentary hearings on Tuesday.
"The president is concerned by elements of confrontation on the public political stage, moreover confrontation between members of the same team," Yastrzhembsky said.

"In connection with this Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) ordered the prime minister, the Security Council secretary and the interior minister to agree their position before closed hearings start in the State Duma on the Chechen problems."
He added: "As far as I know this order has been carried out."
The Duma was debating Chechnya on Tuesday. Details of the closed session were not immediately available.

Security Council secretary Lebed signed a peace deal with Chechen separatist leaders on August 31. Russia promised to withdraw troops and both sides agreed to postpone a decision on the region's future political status for five years.

Other officials, including Kulikov, have criticised the deal, saying Chechnya must remain part of Russia. On Monday, Yeltsin named Lebed as the head of a team to lead further talks with the Chechen separatists.
The divisions over Chechnya have widened while Yeltsin is out of the Kremlin preparing for heart surgery. Some ex-Kremlin officials have also traded charges of high-level corruption in the past week.
"The president knows about all these verbal duels, accusations and counter-charges," Yastrzhembsky said.
Although Yeltsin was worried, it was too soon to say what conclusions he had drawn from the rivalry, Yastrzhembsky said.
